2. Get API key → Create API key.

keys.guide.google-cloud:
The Chirp 3 HD voices (Google Cloud Text-to-Speech) work two ways; choose above:
• Sign in with Google (recommended): you create a 'Desktop app' client in your own Google Cloud project; the steps show here while 'Sign in with Google' is chosen.
• API key: 1. Create a project at console.cloud.google.com and link billing. 2. APIs & Services → Library → enable "Cloud Text-to-Speech API". 3. Credentials → Create credentials → API key; restrict it to the Text-to-Speech API. 4. Paste the key and press "Save and test the connection" (tested with a free voice listing). Google's documents show only OAuth for this API; if the key is refused, sign in with Google.
With both, the Google sign-in is used.
keys.guide.elevenlabs:
For the ElevenLabs voices (v4, v4 Turbo, Flash):
1. Open elevenlabs.io and sign in.
2. Choose a plan (API use is paid per character).
3. Settings → API Keys → Create API key.
4. Copy the key and paste it here.
5. Press "Save and test the connection" (tested with a free voice listing). Once saved, the voices of your account (cloned and library voices too) are read in the background; "Refresh voices" in the voice picker reads them again.

keys.guide.endpoint:
Any server that speaks the OpenAI API: a program on your computer, your own server on your network or the internet, or a service that offers an OpenAI-compatible address. Its models are then offered in every text step.
Ollama and LM Studio on this computer are found by themselves: they show under "Found on this computer"; press Add. Their own address is enough (no /v1): the app then lists their installed models, sets the context, and unloads the model when an image or voice model needs the graphics card. For LM Studio, start its server first (Developer tab, or: lms server start).
1. Start the server and load a model (for a remote service, get its address and API key).
2. Type its address; if the server needs a key, put it in the token field, otherwise leave it empty. Press "Connect and list models".
3. Tick the models to use (or type an id if it is not listed), check their context and answer limits, save.
Common addresses:
• Ollama: http://localhost:11434
• LM Studio: http://localhost:1234
• Lemonade Server: http://localhost:13305/api/v1 (older versions: port 8000)
• llama.cpp llama-server: http://localhost:8080/v1 (new builds: port 9931)
• vLLM: http://localhost:8000/v1
• Another computer on your network: http://192.168.1.20:8080/v1
• A remote server or service: https://your-server.example.com/v1 + API key
Little graphics memory: Ollama runs what does not fit from main memory by itself (slower); in LM Studio lower "GPU Offload" in the model's settings (or lms load <model> --gpu 0.5).
AMD graphics cards: Ollama and LM Studio use Vulkan or ROCm; Lemonade Server, or llama.cpp's ROCm or Vulkan builds, also run models on them.
Cost: the app records no price for custom servers; if a remote service charges, watch the spending in that service's dashboard.

keys.endpoint.models_tip: Context = the context size the server runs the model with (llama-server: its -c value); a call never asks for more answer than the context leaves next to its prompt. Max answer = the most tokens one answer may have (a step that asks more gets this); the video code step needs a large one (tens of thousands of tokens), so give the model a large context. Reads images: offered for describing sample images. JSON schema: tick only if the server accepts response_format json_schema (LM Studio, vLLM, recent llama.cpp); otherwise JSON mode is asked. Ollama and LM Studio: the context is what the app loads the model with (a larger one takes more graphics memory); their models take a JSON schema.

keys.endpoint.note.ollama: Ollama: the app sends the context with every request and unloads the model from the graphics card when an image or voice model needs it. If the model and its context do not fit in the card's memory, Ollama runs the rest from main memory by itself (it works, but slower); "Test connection" shows how much is where. A smaller model or a smaller context fits better.
keys.endpoint.note.lmstudio: LM Studio: the app loads the model with this context and unloads it from the graphics card when an image or voice model needs it. LM Studio decides itself how much goes on the card; if a model does not fit, lower "GPU Offload" in its model settings in LM Studio (or load it once with: lms load <model> --gpu 0.5).
keys.endpoint.think_tip: The model thinks before it answers: often better, but slower and the answer limit has to hold the thinking too. Off: it answers at once.

report.title: Report a problem
report.intro: Nothing is sent automatically. TM Concept has no telemetry: you decide what to share, and you attach it yourself.
report.contains:
“Prepare logs” makes a zip file in the data folder (reports) and shows it. It contains:
• the log files of the last 7 days. Before they go in, your home folder, the app's folders, e-mail addresses and keys are masked, and while the app is unlocked every profile name and concept or video title it knows becomes <name> (the activity lines of 0.1.4 leave them out already)
• system.txt: version, operating system, architecture, .NET, interface language, drawing mode and which tools are installed
It never contains your database, API keys, concept or narration texts, or video files. The logs do say which settings you changed and to what (interface language, drawing mode, notifications, each step's model, effort and engine). Masking is a safety net, not a guarantee: open the zip and read it before you share it publicly.
report.steps: “Report on GitHub” opens the issue form in your browser with the version and the system filled in: describe what happened and drag the zip into the form (a GitHub account is needed). “Copy details” copies the system information to the clipboard.

speech.pocket.note: Pocket TTS (Kyutai): free, runs on this computer, English only; it speaks with your own voice added in Settings → Voice and pronunciation. The speed setting has no effect on this voice. Weights CC-BY-4.0: when you publish, write "Voice: Pocket TTS, Kyutai (CC-BY-4.0)" in the description. Whose voice you copy is your responsibility.
speech.chatterbox.note: Chatterbox Multilingual V3 (Resemble AI): free, runs on this computer, speaks Turkish, English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Polish and Swedish with your own voice added in Settings → Voice and pronunciation. It runs on the processor only (the graphics card is not used): about 6 times as long as the speech on a 16-thread processor (longer with fewer cores), so a 5-minute narration takes about half an hour. The first scene also waits about 1.5 minutes while the model loads. The speed setting has no effect on this voice. MIT license, no watermark: say that the voice is AI-generated when you publish. Whose voice you copy is your responsibility.
speech.ahenk-cep.note: Ahenk Cep: free, runs on this computer, Turkish only. One voice with seven speaking styles (neutral, calm, cheerful, empathetic, sad, angry, surprised). The model is about 13 MB and runs on the processor only (the graphics card is not used); a minute of speech takes about 10 seconds. The app reads numbers, dates and abbreviations out before it speaks. Licensed CC BY 4.0: say that the voice is AI-generated when you publish and credit it in the description ("Voice: Ahenk Cep (CC BY 4.0)").

storage.explain: What the app keeps on this computer: downloaded programs and models, work caches, backups and logs. Remove what you no longer use; it is downloaded again when a setting needs it.
storage.explain.more: "Used by" comes from every profile's saved model choices (and what the app itself needs, such as ffmpeg). Everything you remove is deleted permanently, after you confirm it with its size. Models, documents and library files without a record go only when you tick them. Nothing is removed while a video, a generation, a narration or an install runs. Your database, profiles, concepts, videos, backups and logs are never removed here.
storage.clean.tip: Deletes the tools no profile uses and space that comes back by itself: unfinished downloads, old component folders, and cached narration and work folders older than 7 days. Nothing that is in use; models and documents only when you tick them.

styles.explain: A template says how videos look and end: subtitles, progress bar, font, title style and position, colours, the drawing style of scenes without images, motion and the closing call to action. Templates belong to this computer, not to a profile. Choose one on the Concept to video page; each video takes a copy when it starts, so editing or deleting a template never changes a video already made.

styles.word_highlight.tip: The word being said shows in the accent colour, so the eye follows the voice. The highlight matches the style: it glows in neon, hologram and terminal, the word grows a little in the flat, cartoon and stick-figure looks, and only its colour changes in the drawn and paper looks. With whisper.cpp installed the word lights up when it is really said; without it, words share their sentence's time by their length.

styles.word_times.tip: With whisper.cpp (a free program, about 9 MB, and its multilingual model, about 148 MB) the narration of each video is heard once on this computer and every subtitle word gets the time it is really said: the highlight sits on the right word and the subtitles break where the voice takes a breath. The text always stays your narration's; the hearing is only a ruler. A sentence that matches poorly is listed with "check by ear". Nothing is downloaded until you say yes; it applies to every template.

styles.readable.tip: On (the default): subtitles and on-screen text get an outline and a soft shadow in the colour opposite to the text (black under light text, white under dark text), so they stay readable over an image or a background of their own colour.
styles.progress.tip: On: the app draws a thin bar in the accent colour that fills up as the video plays. Off (the default): no progress bar, timer or scene counter; a video code that draws one is sent back for repair.

styles.palette.tip: The six colours of the video: background, surface (bands, cards), accent, second accent, text and quiet text. The video code may use only these; a stray colour is replaced by the nearest one.
styles.emphasis.tip: Weight and slant of the text. Automatic: bold titles, regular text, bold subtitles (as before). Any other choice is used for titles, on-screen text and subtitles; a font without an italic face is slanted.
styles.font.tip: For titles, on-screen text and subtitles. The fonts that come with the app are free (SIL Open Font License) and have the Turkish letters; Tinos is a classic serif with the widths of Times New Roman. Fonts installed on this computer (Times New Roman, Georgia…) are listed after them: a video made here uses them, another computer falls back to Fira Sans. A Russian video needs a font with Cyrillic letters (Fira Sans, Tinos), otherwise Fira Sans is used.
styles.title_position.tip: Where the scene titles sit on the picture.
styles.draw.tip: The look of the video: how the video code draws a scene without an image, which style generated images are asked for and the style's own motion rules. "Let the AI choose" (the default of a new template): the model picks the style that fits each video's topic. Some styles (Stick-figure narrator) also change how the concept is written: Concepts page, Fine-tuning → Drawing style.
styles.draw.prefers_images: Looks best with an image model; code alone draws it only roughly.
styles.motion.tip: How much things move: calm, normal or lively.
styles.tempo.tip: The breathing room the narration leaves after sentences and between scenes. Tight: short breaks. Natural: a clear pause after every sentence and a longer one at a scene change. Relaxed: long pauses, a calm narration.
styles.drawer.tip: Who draws the video (HyperFrames only). The app: the model writes only each scene's plan (picture, map, diagram or title; routes, arrows, pins, labels, counters, the camera; one step per sentence) and the app's own library draws it — steadier and cheaper. Free code: the model writes the animation's code itself (anything goes, but it costs more and sometimes breaks).
styles.finish.tip: When the app draws, it lays a finishing layer that fits the drawing style over the scenes: paper texture, grain, darker corners (vignette), glow, shadow by depth and a slight tremble in 12 steps a second. The style sets which effects and how strong; no extra AI request, rendering takes a little longer. Works only with Drawn by = The app and a chosen style. On in new templates; off in earlier ones (their videos stay as they were).
styles.closing.tip: A short sentence at the end that asks viewers to subscribe or follow. Always in the video's language (ready sentences, no model writes them). Voice: the sentence is added to the end of the last scene's narration. Screen: an end card in the last seconds with the profile's channel photo (if it has one), the channel name and the sentence.

style.draw.auto.desc: No style given: for each video the model picks the style that fits its topic and scenes (one of the list or its own description). The chosen style is kept in the video's details.
style.draw.flat.desc: Plain flat-coloured shapes and icons; shapes come in with a short pop. A safe choice for explainers.
style.draw.stickfigure.desc: A stick-figure narrator stands in the scene, talks, points and reacts, next to drawings and diagrams of the subject. When concepts are written for this style, their scenes are the narrator's actions.
style.draw.lineart.desc: Thin one-colour lines that draw on along their length, with a faint paper texture.
style.draw.papercut.desc: Layered paper cut-outs; pieces slide in to their place and keep a fixed shadow, with a paper texture.
style.draw.infographic.desc: Big numbers, charts, icons and arrows; bars grow from zero, numbers count up.
style.draw.neon.desc: Glowing lines on a dark background that draw on, with a faint film grain.
style.draw.pencilsketch.desc: Pencil on warm paper: a light construction line first, then the dark line, shading by hatching; one accent colour, on the subject only.
style.draw.cartoon.desc: A 2D cartoon look: bold outlines, flat cel shading, rounded friendly forms; squash and stretch on entrances.
style.draw.blueprint.desc: White technical drawing on blue: outlines, sections, dimension arrows and a fine grid, drawn on line by line. Suits technology and engineering.
style.draw.hologram.desc: Glowing cyan wireframes, rings and readout panels on a dark screen, with a gentle flicker and scanlines. Suits science and the future.
style.draw.terminal.desc: Phosphor-green characters on a black CRT: shapes built from letters, text typed in letter by letter, scanlines.
style.draw.isometric.desc: Small isometric blocks and buildings at 30 degrees; each object draws its outline first, then its faces fill in.
style.draw.watercolor.desc: Soft wet-edged washes on textured paper over a thin pencil line; colours bloom in slowly.
style.draw.pixelart.desc: Chunky retro-game pixels: the scene on a small grid blown up four times, colours from ramps of the palette, shading by dithering; scenes change by a dither dissolve, an iris or blocks. Works without pictures too.

localai.explain: TM Concept can install and run its own copy of Ollama, so text models run on your computer for free, without an API key.
localai.explain.more: Ollama (TM Concept) is the official Ollama release, downloaded only after you confirm it. After unpacking, only the graphics part your card needs is kept (NVIDIA CUDA 12 or 13, Vulkan for AMD and Intel, or none for the processor). It runs on 127.0.0.1 on a port of its own (never 11434), keeps its models in the app's data folder, loads one model at a time and ends when TM Concept closes. An Ollama or LM Studio you run yourself stays separate: add it under Settings → Keys if you want to use it.

localai.runtime.note: This is the app's own copy: it never touches an Ollama you installed yourself. Remove it or its models in Settings → Storage.

An orange license limits commercial use. Nothing is downloaded before you confirm; installed models show up in the model choice of every text step.

documents.title: From documents
documents.tip: Concepts that rest only on your own documents (PDF, Word, text, Markdown, a web page or a Wikipedia article in any language). Add them under "My documents". A subject is optional. Write N concepts at once, or find N topics in the documents first and write one concept per ticked topic. The concepts are written in the video's language even when the documents are in another one, and each names the documents it used.

help.settings.language: The language of the app's menus, buttons and messages. It changes at once, no restart needed. The language of your videos is set per profile, on the Profile page.

Only the project's release list on GitHub is read and nothing about you is sent. A new version is downloaded only after you confirm it. "What's new" shows the notes of every version, also offline.

help.backup.now: Writes an encrypted backup file at once with what you tick. Use it before a big change or to move to another computer. Restoring is possible only in the first-run window, before there is any data.

help.install: Downloads and installs what your settings need, from official sources, into the app's own tools folder. Programs and models are checked against pinned SHA-256 values. Cancel stops after the running download; what finished stays installed.
help.appupdate: Lists the notes of every version since yours; only the newest one is installed. The download is checked against its SHA-256 before it replaces the app, then the app restarts. "Later" keeps your version.

You are running the portable program. Installed, TM Concept gets Start menu and desktop shortcuts, can be removed from Windows' Apps list, and its updates download only what changed. Nothing changes in your data: both use the same folder.

styles.music.generate.local.tip: Two local options. ACE-Step 1.5 through rakkase (both MIT; its text encoder Qwen3-Embedding, Apache-2.0): a real music model made for NVIDIA cards; on a 4 GB card it was measured at about 2.6 GB; its Python packages and weights are large. Program composes (music from code): no model and no graphics card, it runs on any computer in seconds; the app writes the notes itself from the words of the prompt (mood, style, tempo) and a synthesizer plays them with the MuseScore General instruments (spessasynth_core, Apache-2.0; SoundFont MIT, about 40 MB). styles.quality.tip: Fast (default): the video is made as before, no extra request. Standard: after the render, a model that reads images (the 'Quality check' step on the video page: local and free, such as Gemma 3 4B, or online and paid) looks at the start, middle and end of every scene and its beats on one sheet in ONE request and names the problems: blocker = seen at normal speed, polish = only when enlarged. A final critic then scores the video under fixed headings 1–5 in ONE more request; below 4 is marked 'does not pass'. Nothing is changed, it is a report (video details on the Produced page and the activity panel). Careful: the same, plus repair rounds: when Drawn by = The app, only the faulty scene's plan is asked again (one small plan request per faulty scene, paid by the video code model) and the video is rendered again; at most 3 reviews, after the 2nd only blockers count, and it stops when the list does not shrink. With Free code it only warns. Careful also draws a sheet of a recurring character (one more picture) and compares the pictures with it (one more request); pictures made on this computer and reviewed by a local model are made again when faulty. Every request of the mode is in the estimate (the high end is the worst case).
step.quality-check.purpose: Used only when the chosen template's quality mode is Standard or Careful: a model that reads images reviews the rendered frames and scores the video. It can be another model than the one that writes the plan: a local one (free, on this computer; such as Gemma 3 4B) or an online one (paid per request; its cost is in the estimate). Off: the quality mode does nothing (a yellow warning).

styles.reference.tip: "Make it at the tempo of this video": pick a video file or paste the address of one video and measure it. The app measures how often it cuts, how much and which way its camera moves, its colours, its beat and its strongest moments, and keeps only these numbers (no picture, frame or sound of it). Every video of this profile asks the scene plan for the same number of changes, camera moves and eases, with emphasis moments at the same places; the narration's tempo is set to the preset nearest to the reference. Only the first 10 minutes are measured.

Use videos you are allowed to view; nothing is shared.

music.make.tip: Write what you want in your own words: "ancient Egyptian music for the mystery of Egypt", "disco in ancient Egypt". The models understand English descriptions best. The piece goes into My music; on the Concept to video page choose it with the "My music" source.

music.model.tip: Program composes: free, any computer, no model; the app writes the notes from your words (it knows moods such as calm, epic, sad, tense, mysterious, happy and styles such as orchestral, electronic, ambient, acoustic, pop, world, medieval, in English or Turkish) and plays them with General MIDI instruments; the same words give another piece each time. ACE-Step 1.5: a real music model, free, for NVIDIA cards. Google Lyria and ElevenLabs Music: paid, with your own key. A model that is not installed is installed after one confirmation when you press Make.
